clue.text: Dairy product person in society fed to pet

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it, so one word ends up within the other

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
someone belonging to a society is one of its members

explanation.surface: Someone at a society function is slipping cheese to the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dairy product' sits up front as the definition; 'fed to pet' reads as feeding the cat, but it is the instruction to put one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, one example of produce from a dairy.

clue.text: Nursery care avoided by a revolutionary

indicators.note: the word that is avoided keeps clear of the letter that follows, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed from the word before it
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A childcare report: the nursery's care was shunned by a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE without its A leaves CRE; Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are looked after while parents work.

clue.text: No time for human message from story

indicators.note: saying no to something refuses it entry, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: a human being is a mortal
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Reads like a complaint that busy people have no time to absorb a story's lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: MORTAL with its T taken away leaves MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a fable is the lesson or teaching that the tale is meant to convey.

clue.text: Turned tail when collared by new activist

indicators.note: a collar wraps round a neck, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: something brand new is in mint condition

indicators.note: turned suggests something rearranged or twisted round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A protester who fled was arrested by the police, pictured as a tail-turning radical being collared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned tail' wants to mean ran away; here turned only signals rearranging the word tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant is a campaigner who takes forceful or aggressive action for a cause.

clue.text: One specialist disposing of sixteen twerps?

indicators.note: disposing can mean arranging or setting out, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: One expert dismissing sixteen idiots, as if clearing a room of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: an expert witness gives a deposition, and 'disposing' plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert witness is a single professional called to court to give specialist opinion evidence.

clue.text: Warmer weather that cut short start of winter

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims its final letter

parts.note: the word that without its last letter

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of winter

explanation.surface: Milder weather that brought an early end to the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw is a spell of warmer weather in which ice and snow melt.

clue.text: Best score at snooker recalled

indicators.note: calling something back sends it the other way, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a snooker player scores by potting a ball

explanation.surface: A commentator remembering the finest break at a snooker match.
explanation.definitionFit: Top as an adjective means highest or finest, the same as best.

clue.text: Source of hurricane in printing error about storm

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a typo is a typing or printing mistake

indicators.note: the source of something is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of hurricane
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A newspaper misprint in a story about a hurricane's origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the containment instruction, but it supplies its own letters, the sense of on as in a talk on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone, a violent storm of the western Pacific.

clue.text: Fruit basket appearing in online joke community?

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a net, short for network, is a connected community; online points to the internet sense

explanation.surface: A fruit basket that has become a running gag in some internet forum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online joke community' reads as one phrase, but online and community together give NET while joke sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small light container in which soft fruit such as strawberries is sold in Britain.

clue.text: Recalled learning about new record

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the whole is read the other way
about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: lore is accumulated knowledge or learning
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone remembering their studies about a fresh record.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside LORE gives LORNE, which reversed reads ENROL. 'Recalled learning' looks like remembered study; recalled is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to register or enter a name on an official list, as record means as a verb.

clue.text: Entertainment for kids by drama writer

parts.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A children's show by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a playpen is where small children are left to amuse themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is an enclosure where toddlers safely play, so it keeps young children amused.

clue.text: Time not at school felt unsettled amidst damage

indicators.note: amidst places one piece in the middle of another

parts.note: harm is damage

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed and out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil feeling anxious about the destruction around them during a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Half term is a short British school holiday midway through a term; 'felt' looks like a verb about feelings but is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Half term is a brief holiday in the middle of a British school term, when pupils stay home.

clue.text: Single copy not initiated

indicators.note: something not initiated has not been begun, so its opening letter is missing

parts.note: a clone is an exact copy

explanation.surface: A lone duplicate that was never started.
explanation.definitionFit: Lone means solitary or only one, as in a lone survivor.

clue.text: I concede accepting negative comment will be foolish

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it in, holding it within

parts.note: to grant a point is to concede it
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Someone admits that taking criticism on board would be unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I concede' reads as an admission, but I stands alone and concede is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant describes someone lacking knowledge, close enough to senseless or unwise to stand in for foolish.

clue.text: Group continue to swing in popular trend

parts.note: a band is a group, such as of musicians
to wag is to swing to and fro, like a tail
to carry on is to continue

explanation.surface: A musical group keeps on swinging, following the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continue to swing' is read with the verb first in the answer and the carrying-on word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a fashionable movement that many people join to share its success.

clue.text: Composer plagued by mosquitoes crossing river

indicators.note: crossing here means straddling, with one piece spread around another

parts.note: someone plagued by mosquitoes has been bitten
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A composer is pestered by insects while fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a 20th-century English composer; 'crossing' suggests fording but means spanning one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was an English composer of operas such as Peter Grimes.

clue.text: Leap year's subdivision?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the four seasons

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leap year' reads as one phrase about February 29th; split it, and each part is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is both a bounding jump and the season between winter and summer that forms part of a year.

clue.text: Industry finally supporting shop floor

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of industry

explanation.surface: A business propping up the trading floor of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Storey is the British spelling for one level of a building, a synonym of floor in that sense.

clue.text: Piano melody or two

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A piano tune, or perhaps a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two matching things or people.

clue.text: Refused to participate and became prominent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kept out of something, abstained
second meaning: was conspicuous or noticeable

explanation.surface: A refusenik whose refusal made them famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both declined to join in and was clearly noticeable among others.

clue.text: Musical instrument helping to sustain a group, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters run the other way
helping to sustain means forming a part of these words, held within them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of sustain, a and the start of group

explanation.surface: Music keeps a band going, one realises after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found across sustaiN A GROup and read backwards to give ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a keyboard instrument sounded by air through pipes.

clue.text: Move slowly in church

parts.note: taken as written; that the two words also spell the answer outright is a coincidence of the charade
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Shuffling down a church aisle at a wedding pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to edge forward by tiny amounts, a little at a time.

clue.text: I note past, present or future could be deeply emotional

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for note
each is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that every stage of life stirs strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past, present or future' looks like a span of time but is a grammar term naming each one.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and passionate, so an intense person is deeply emotional.

clue.text: Daughter escaping peril shows passion

indicators.note: something escaping gets out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: peril is danger
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl fleeing danger reveals her strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion can mean a fit of rage or fury, which is strong anger.

clue.text: Send back negative information

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: neg is the short form of negative; that these are its opening letters is a coincidence of the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone returning unwanted bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in the full gen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is informal British slang for facts or details on a subject.

clue.text: Doubtful behaviour is wrong in any ethics

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the letters it covers are jumbled

parts.note: all nine letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A moral pronouncement that wavering conduct is an error in any ethical system.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitancy is indecision or reluctance, conduct showing uncertainty about acting.
